# Independent production updater-daemon observation

These eight raw files came from the **unchanged Python** `rust/tools/check_updated_daemon.py` invocation in [Actions run 39552685601, job 119065236839](https://github.com/bin9208/openpilot-rust/actions/runs/39552685601/job/119065236839). The diagnostic workflow head was `47248011fce3758e89201db82bac47f7b2aa700d`; the job explicitly checked out source `19e47ad98286edb1b572b146a85304e1e94e4edf`. Artifact `12323934751` had ZIP SHA-256 `999ee5d1df557e5d0c16cd063a3d1db827b95ace00b9004b0c10fd2b9c83e21c`. `SHA256SUMS` records the artifact members without editing their bytes. Its own SHA-256 is embedded in the Rust retirement test.

The original invocation was bounded by UTC Unix nanoseconds `1792562491512826293` and `1792562492873864873`, recorded by the job before and after the Python command. The source file SHA-256 was `82be3830f8e468c32abe583c197cdf2777cd5fb748a795a8c70247a7dcd00059`; the retained helper `updated_fixtures.py` SHA-256 was `76607e02520f383227264257de0ed8505b9dc12e462227b176f2c919dfec2d60`. No Python source is stored here.

The Rust comparison checks the complete report, all 16 Params values, all 22 log records, ordered overlay commands, raw daemon and duplicate logs, and stdout/stderr. Only the three observed wall-clock Params, producer/process metadata, the validated fixture-parent path in one Git-fetch message, the LFS-duration number, and the runtime source commit may vary. Each variable field is checked for shape or range before normalization. The two producer threads retain their own full record order; cross-thread arrival order is not an invariant.

Before removing `check_updated_daemon.py`, Actions must run one native checker ELF and the same held daemon, launcher, and fixture ELFs against both checkout-present and private-checker-absent roots. Retain both `strace` traces, reject unsuccessful, unfinished, `execveat`, and unknown executable attempts, seal executable bytes before and after, and compare both full outcomes to these original-only files. After deletion, require both roots absent. `updated_fixtures.py` is separately live through `updated_check.rs` and remains out of this deletion.

The original CLI admission capture is a separate prerequisite. In hosted Actions, run unchanged Python 3.12 with an explicit timeout for the eleven cases named in `updated_daemon_cli.rs`; record each raw argument byte string as hex, exit code, stdout/stderr hex, original source SHA-256, interpreter path/hash, and checked-out source commit in an immutable original-only JSON receipt. Include the non-UTF-8 `--binary` value before `--help`; if the host cannot execute it, record that case pending and do not claim complete CLI admission. The native CLI test requires the receipt and its SHA-256. Pin that SHA-256 in source policy before Python deletion; do not synthesize expected outcomes from native output.

Help alone does not prove a valid raw path. The separate hosted `capture_updated_daemon_raw_output.py` runs the unchanged original with a real `--output` path ending in byte `0xff`, copies its complete six-file result into an ASCII-named original-only evidence directory, and retains raw stdout/stderr plus an independently hashed manifest with the original invocation window. The retirement test then executes the native CLI with its own actual non-UTF-8 output path and compares the full result, 16 Params, 22 structured log records, ordered overlay commands, raw daemon and duplicate logs, stdout, and stderr. Before deleting Python, pin the new raw manifest SHA and preserve its eight member hashes; the valid raw-path lane is mandatory alongside the two same-ELF source-presence lanes.

Every record's `created` value must be finite and within its own capture window before normalization. The native controller holds the five private `git`, `bash`, `ionice`, `find`, and `sudo` symlinks and native-host ELF targets through final receipt publication. The proof binds the before/after alias receipts to held executable hashes and private exec paths. This admission covers those private aliases and the separately audited system executable roster; it does not infer interpreter behavior from a program name.
